newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PSE moves up mass de-listing to March 31.
newsitem.headline: Czech PSE moves up mass de-listing to March 31.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) said on Tuesday that moves to delist 800 to 900 low-liquidity shares from the PSE would be brought forward, with the first 400 facing the chop on March 31.
Jiri Franc, general secretary of the PSE, also told a news conference that another 400-500 shares could be cut in the next wave of cuts which should be completed in June.
The PSE anounced in January that it would downsize the exchange starting at the end of March with 100 issues and completing the first batch of 400 by the end of June.
The exchange is looking at shares which fell into the following three categories according to activity over the last 12 months:
1) Those whose trade turnover was below 200,000 crowns ($7,160).
2) Those with a market capitalisation under five million crowns.
3) Those which have failed to trade for more than five days. Issues which fail to fulfil conditions one and two or one and three would be eligible for de-listing.

There are currently 1,751 shares on the PSE, many of which are small companies which were listed as a direct result of the Czech Republic's massive voucher-for-shares privatisation programme completed in early 1995.
